names.official: Income tax paid by individuals

taxes.base: Income of individuals taxable in Malta: employment, business and other income.
taxes.payer: Individuals; employers withhold tax from wages.

rate.headline: 0% to 35%
details: Income is taxable at graduated progressive rates ranging from 0% to 35% (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 30 September 2026), not checked against the Commissioner for Revenue.

instruments.explanation: EUR 1.6 billion in 2024: the largest direct tax.

names.official: Income tax paid by companies

taxes.base: Profit of companies.

rate.headline: 35% statutory
details: Companies are subject to income tax at a flat rate of 35%; entities may elect a 15% rate on their chargeable income under the FITWI Regulations published on 2 September 2025 (PwC). Refunds to shareholders are a feature of the Maltese system; the National Tax List does not say whether this line is before or after them.
As summarised by PwC (review of 30 September 2026), not checked against the Commissioner for Revenue.

names.official: Taxes on holding gains of individuals and of companies

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List: holding gains by individuals (EUR 123.0 million) and by companies (EUR 125.8 million).

rate.headline: Set by the Income Tax Act

names.official: Penalties paid by individuals, companies and others

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List: penalties paid by individuals (EUR 4.5 million), companies (EUR 6.9 million) and others (EUR 0.1 million).

instruments.explanation: The list books these penalties among taxes on income.

names.official: Individual (International) Investor Programme

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List: the fees of the Individual Investor Programme (citizenship by investment).

instruments.explanation: EUR 148.5 million in 2024, about 2% of the taxes and contributions.

names.official: Employers’ social contributions (private sector and government) and penalties on employers

taxes.base: The employee’s basic weekly wage, within a minimum and maximum. Private sector EUR 410.6 million, government as employer EUR 84.3 million, penalties EUR 5.1 million.

rate.headline: 10% of the basic weekly wage
details: Social security contributions amount to 10% of the employee’s basic weekly wage, payable by both the employee and the employer, subject to a minimum and maximum contribution (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 30 September 2026), not checked against the Commissioner for Revenue.

instruments.explanation: The Treasury Department’s service pension (EUR 106.7 million), which the list treats as an imputed contribution, is not counted.

names.official: Employees’ social contributions

taxes.base: The employee’s basic weekly wage, within a minimum and maximum.

rate.headline: 10% of the basic weekly wage
details: The maximum weekly contribution is EUR 49.04 for employees born before 1 January 1962 and EUR 55.93 for those born later (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 30 September 2026), not checked against the Commissioner for Revenue.

names.official: Social contributions of the self-employed and penalties
names.native: Kontribuzzjonijiet tas-sigurtà soċjali tal-ħaddiema għal rashom

taxes.base: Annual net income of the self-employed, within a minimum and maximum.

rate.headline: 15% of net annual income
details: Contributions amount to 15% of the self-employed person’s annual net income of the previous year, within a minimum and maximum (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 30 September 2026), not checked against the Commissioner for Revenue.

names.official: Value added tax

taxes.base: Goods and services supplied in Malta and imports.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and claim input credits.

rate.headline: 18% standard; 7% and 5% reduced
details: The standard VAT rate is 18%; 7% applies to eligible accommodation and entrance to sports facilities, 5% to electricity, printed matter and other supplies (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 30 September 2026), not checked against the Commissioner for Revenue.

instruments.explanation: EUR 1.4 billion: the largest indirect tax.

names.official: Import duties paid to EU institutions

taxes.base: Goods imported from outside the EU, by the Common Customs Tariff.

rate.headline: EU Common Customs Tariff
details: An EU own resource; Eurostat records it under the EU institutions.

names.official: Excise levies on petroleum

taxes.base: Petrol, diesel and other petroleum products, by quantity.
taxes.payer: Fuel suppliers; passed on at the pump.

names.official: Excise levies on machine-made cigarettes and other tobacco

taxes.base: Cigarettes (EUR 95.4 million) and other tobacco (EUR 8.3 million).
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Fixed by the Excise Duty Act

legalRefs.locator: sheet MT, D214A C01 and C05

names.official: Excise levies and duties on alcohol, cement, electricity, mobile telephony services and a range of products

taxes.base: Spirits (EUR 18.0 million), cement (EUR 20.7 million), beer, wines, electricity (EUR 4.3 million), mobile telephony (EUR 4.2 million), non-alcoholic beverages, tyres, plastic bags, bottled water, toiletries, construction components, chewing gum and the eco contribution.

names.official: Duty on documents: immovable property and property transfers

taxes.base: Documents transferring immovable property (EUR 141.7 million) and other property transfers (EUR 37.5 million, booked as a capital tax).

legalRefs.locator: sheet MT, D214C C01, D91A C03

names.official: Duty on documents: insurance policies, shares and legal fees
names.native: Dritt fuq id-dokumenti (polza, ishma, drittijiet legali)
names.common: Duty on documents: insurance and shares

taxes.base: Insurance policies (EUR 39.2 million), shares (EUR 6.5 million) and legal fees.
taxes.payer: Policyholders and parties to the share deals.

rate.headline: A percentage of the value or premium

legalRefs.locator: sheet MT, D214G C01, D214C C02, D214B C03

names.official: Motor vehicle registration tax, motor vehicle licences (households and business), number plates and test administration charge

taxes.base: Registration (EUR 37.6 million), licences for households (EUR 62.1 million) and business (EUR 20.7 million), number plates and the test administration charge.

legalRefs.locator: sheet MT, D214D, D59D C03, D29B, D214H C04

names.official: Gaming taxes and the Malta Gaming Authority service fees

taxes.base: Gaming operators (EUR 74.2 million) and the Authority’s service charges (EUR 11.3 million).

legalRefs.locator: sheet MT, D214F C01 and C02

names.official: Bunkering tax and environmental contribution

taxes.base: Ships’ fuel supplies in Maltese waters (EUR 2.2 million) and the environmental contribution (EUR 6.1 million).

rate.headline: Set by law
details: The sale of emission trading permits (EUR 44.6 million) is not counted.

legalRefs.locator: sheet MT, D214H C05 and C06

names.official: Licences, concessions, rights of use and authority service charges

taxes.base: Fees for the right of use by business (EUR 9.2 million), concession fees (EUR 10.6 million), authority services of the Malta Communications and Malta Resources authorities (EUR 6.5 million), driving licences, hotel and catering licences, wines and spirits licences and others.

names.official: Contributions to Protection Funds

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List; no further detail.
